label: Modal verbs
outcome: Lo studente sceglie e forma can/can't, must/mustn't, have to/don't have to e should/shouldn't in base al significato di abilità/permesso, possibilità semplice, obbligo, divieto, assenza di obbligo e consiglio.
must_master: can/can't for ability and basic permission
can for simple general possibility at programme-appropriate level
must for strong speaker-imposed or immediate obligation
have to / has to for external obligation
don't have to / doesn't have to for absence of obligation
modal verb + base verb without to for can, must and should
present-simple support for have to: do/does, don't/doesn't, has to

scope_boundary.later_modals: Do not teach may/might probability, must/might/can't deduction, should have, could have, must have or other past-modal patterns.
scope_boundary.politeness: Can I...? and Can you...? may appear as basic permission/request support, but this is not a full functional-language politeness course.
scope_boundary.past_and_future_obligation: Do not systematically teach had to, will have to or modal perfects.
scope_boundary.meaning_priority: Form is secondary to meaning distinctions, especially mustn't versus don't have to.

italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: You must to wear a helmet.

italian_learner_risks.risk: confusing prohibition and absence of obligation
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: You mustn't bring a laptop. (= it isn't necessary)
italian_learner_risks.target: You don't have to bring a laptop. (= it isn't necessary)

italian_learner_risks.risk: using should for a compulsory rule
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: Students should show ID at security. (official requirement)
italian_learner_risks.target: Students have to show ID at security.

italian_learner_risks.risk: forgetting has to in third person
italian_learner_risks.example_wrong: She have to leave at six.
italian_learner_risks.target: She has to leave at six.

italian_learner_risks.risk: using do in a can question

context_bank: advice before an exam or trip
asking permission at home or school

requirements: teach meaning contrasts before a form list
contrast mustn't with don't have to explicitly
contrast must with have to at a simple programme-appropriate level
teach modal + base verb and have-to present-simple support
include at least one meaning-based dialogue
majority of items require interpreting meaning
include ability/permission, obligation, prohibition, no obligation and advice
include one third-person has to / doesn't have to decision
increase autonomy from selection to production
word order or question formation-like task
at least one mustn't versus don't have to distinction
approximately 60 percent standard and 40 percent challenge

quality_rejections: a worksheet that tests only which modal comes before a base verb
treating mustn't and don't have to as synonyms
using should for legal or clearly compulsory requirements in answer keys
teaching deduction or modal perfects inside this Year 1-2 recovery topic
questions where two modals are equally defensible because the source of obligation is unclear
artificial distractors that do not represent plausible learner errors
more than two consecutive decontextualised form-only questions
difficulty created by specialised legal or workplace vocabulary
